students were more likely to implement comments that included praise and localization, but they were less likely to implement comments with mitigating praise, a suggested solution to a problem, or a focus on high- or low-level prose.

only 2 features (praise and localization) increased students' likelihood to use peer feedback, while several features (mitigating praise, solutions to problems, and high-proseness) decreased students' likelihood to revise their papers.

the feedback features that increase students' likelihood to revise are not the same features that improve the quality of students' revisions.
